title: Chopin, Étude Op. 25 No. 6: Neeman and Paderewski
work: Étude in G♯ minor, Op. 25 No. 6
question: How do the fast thirds leave room for the slower tune underneath?
intro: The right hand begins with a trill in thirds, two notes sounding together at every turn. The pairs soon race up and down while the left hand carries a slower melody. Chopin writes sotto voce above the notes, so Paderewski and Neeman have to play this fast finger-work in an undertone.

recordings.label: Edward Neeman, c. 2014
recordings.note: Neeman developed a modification to the sostenuto mechanism that allowed the piano’s sostenuto and damper pedals to be combined in new ways.

recordings.label: Ignacy Jan Paderewski, 1923
recordings.note: Four years after serving as Poland’s prime minister, Paderewski recorded this étude in Camden, New Jersey, on 4 May 1923.

passages.label: Thirds above a slower voice
passages.note: The right hand plays paired notes above the slower left-hand line.

passages.label: Left-hand melody beneath thirds
passages.note: The left hand plays a broad melody while the right continues its closely spaced pairs.

passages.label: Scales in pairs
passages.note: The right hand plays thirds up and down the keyboard while the left hand continues its phrase underneath.
